title: The Herald and the Good News
lead: The Hebrew verb basar, "bring news," and the herald (mevasser) who runs with it are what the Greek Bible translates with euangelizomai, the verb behind the New Testament's "gospel" (euangelion; the English word "gospel" has a different, Old English origin). The herald with feet on the mountains appears in Nahum 1:15, Isaiah 40:9 and Isaiah 52:7, and is adapted in Romans 10:15.

sections.b: In war a runner brought word of the result, good or bad (1 Samuel 4:17; 2 Samuel 18:19-27). Nahum 1:15 and Isaiah 52:7 give the runner the news that the oppressor is gone and God reigns. The New Testament takes the same verb for the preaching of Jesus (Luke 4:18; Acts 10:36) and Paul adapts Isaiah 52:7 for the preachers of the gospel (Romans 10:15).
